content.introduction: The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) conducts national monetary policy in the United States by adjusting the target range for the federal funds rate. After each FOMC meeting, the committee announces its decision to either leave the federal funds rate target range unchanged, decrease the federal funds target range, or increase it. The FOMC implements monetary policy by using its monetary policy tools to ensure that market interest rates are at levels consistent with the FOMC’s target. The Fed adjusts two administered rates, interest on reserve balances and ON RRP, to keep the federal funds rate within the target range determined by the FOMC.

The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC)conducts national monetary policy in the United States. Regularly scheduled FOMC meetings conclude with a vote on the stance of monetary policy—including a decision about whether the FOMC will adjust the target range for the federal funds rate. [...] Image 16: Flow of Monetary Policy: The FOMC sets the federal funds target range. Then comes policy implementation, which influences consumers' and producers' spending decisions.
After each FOMC meeting, the FOMC announces its decision to either:

   leave the federal funds rate target range unchanged;
   decrease the federal funds target range, or 
   increase the federal funds target range.

Once the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) adjusts the target range for the federal funds rate, the Federal Reserve uses its monetary policy tools to implement, or carry out, the new stance of policy. In other words, the Fed uses its tools to ensure that market interest rates, especially the federal funds rate, move in the direction of the new target range. That helps steer the economy toward the Fed’s dual mandate goals. [...] Federal Open Market Committee

   Providing Financial Services [...] In short, the Fed adjusts two administered rates, interest on reserve balances and ON RRP, to keep the federal funds rate within the target range determined by the FOMC. And the Fed adjusts the discount rate to serve as a ceiling. The Fed usually adjusts the three administered rates (interest on reserve balances, ON RRP and discount) by the same amount and at the same time so they move up and down together.

…And one more tool is necessary to ensure that these administered rates are effective.

The FOMC is the body of the Federal Reserve System that sets national monetary policy. The FOMC makes all decisions regarding the conduct of open market operations, which affect the federal funds rate (the rate at which depository institutions lend to each other), the size and composition of the Federal Reserve's asset holdings, and communications with the public about the likely future course of monetary policy.
